title: Connectors: how Power Platform apps, flows and agents reach other services
summary: The connector controls, licensing statements and limitations are supported by Microsoft documentation. The advanced connector policy API note should name the allowlist property, and the Set Host URL explanation needs its supporting source added.

claims.claim: Prebuilt connector classification is reached through Security > Settings > Data and privacy > Data policy > policy > Edit Policy > Prebuilt connectors > connector > Move to Business.
claims.quote: under Settings, select Data and privacy ... select the Data policy section ... select a policy, and then select Edit Policy ... Select the Prebuilt connectors step ... select Move to Business

claims.claim: Add-ConnectorsToPolicy -PolicyName <policy GUID> -Classification <General|Confidential|Blocked> -Connectors <connector objects> sets connector classification.
claims.quote: Add-ConnectorsToPolicy [-PolicyName] <String> [-Classification] <String> [-Connectors] <Object[]> ... Allowed values are 'General', 'Confidential', and 'Blocked' ... The policy name (GUID).

claims.claim: Custom connector patterns are reached through Security > Settings > Data and privacy > Data policy > policy > Edit Policy > Custom connectors > Add connector pattern.
claims.quote: You can add new rules by selecting Add connector pattern on the Custom connectors page.

claims.claim: New-PowerAppPolicyUrlPatterns -TenantId <tenant ID> -PolicyName <policy GUID> -NewUrlPatterns <URL patterns object> creates custom connector URL classification rules.
claims.quote: New-PowerAppPolicyUrlPatterns -TenantId <String> -PolicyName <String> -NewUrlPatterns <Object> ... Creates new URL patterns for a DLP policy

claims.claim: Connector action control is reached through Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > policy > Edit policy > Prebuilt connectors > connector > More actions > Configure connectors > Connector actions.
claims.quote: select Security ... select Data and privacy ... select Data policy ... Edit policy ... Prebuilt connectors ... More actions ... Select Configure connectors and then Connector actions.

claims.claim: New-PowerAppDlpPolicyConnectorConfigurations -TenantId <tenant ID> -PolicyName <policy GUID> -NewDlpPolicyConnectorConfigurations <connector configurations> sets connector action rules.
claims.quote: New-PowerAppDlpPolicyConnectorConfigurations -TenantId $TenantId -PolicyName $PolicyName -NewDlpPolicyConnectorConfigurations $ConnectorConfigurations

claims.claim: Environment group ACP configuration is reached through Manage > Environment groups > environment group > Rules > Advanced connector policies.
claims.quote: select Manage ... select Environment groups ... select the environment group ... Select the Rules tab. ... Select Advanced connector policies.

claims.claim: POST https://api.powerplatform.com/governance/ruleBasedPolicies?api-version=2024-10-01 creates an ACP with connector and action allowlist settings.
claims.quote: $apiBaseUrl = "https://api.powerplatform.com" ... $apiVersion = "2024-10-01" ... Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post ... "$apiBaseUrl/governance/ruleBasedPolicies?api-version=$apiVersion"
claims.fix: Keep the call. Add to controls[3].note and its rendered note: 'The request body sets ruleSets[].inputs.AllowedConnectorList in the ConnectorManagement rule set; entries use AllowedConnector, AllowedActionsMode and AllowedActions to select connectors and actions.'

claims.claim: Tenant-level data policies require Power Platform Administrator permissions.
claims.quote: for tenant-level policies, sign in as a user with the Power Platform Administrator role.

claims.claim: Environment-level policies require Environment Admin permissions, subject to the Dataverse qualification stated in the governance prose.
claims.quote: you need to have Power Apps Environment Admin permissions. For environments with a Dataverse database, you need to be assigned the System Administrator role instead.

claims.claim: General, Confidential and Blocked map respectively to Non-business, Business and Blocked.
claims.quote: Allowed values are 'General', 'Confidential', and 'Blocked' (for Non-business, Business, and Blocked, respectively).

claims.claim: The URL pattern cmdlet is enabled only for tenant-level policies.
claims.quote: Currently, this cmdlet is only enabled for polices at the tenant level.

claims.claim: Environment-level data policies classify custom connectors by name.
claims.quote: You can classify custom connectors by name in environment-level data policies and by host URL pattern in tenant-level data policies.

claims.claim: Classic connector action control is unavailable for unblockable and custom connectors.
claims.quote: You can configure connector actions for all blockable connectors, but not for unblockable connectors and custom connectors.

claims.claim: Individual triggers in classic connector action control are configurable only through PowerShell.
claims.quote: Support for allowing and blocking individual triggers is currently available only via PowerShell.

claims.claim: Administrators need Power Apps maker access to retrieve connector actions.
claims.quote: Admins need to have maker access to Power Apps ... If the admin doesn't have access to Power Apps, then the list of connector actions won't be retrieved.

claims.claim: Environment group rules must be published after saving ACP settings.
claims.quote: select Save ... After you update all rules to your requirements, select Publish rules in the command bar.

claims.claim: Single-environment ACP configuration is reached through Security > Data and privacy > Advanced connector policies.
claims.quote: select Security ... select Data and privacy. ... Select Advanced connector policies.

claims.claim: A second POST assigns the created ACP to an environment group.
claims.quote: Adding ACP to an environment group is a two-part operation: create the policy, then assign it to the group. ... Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post ... /environmentGroups/$environmentGroupId/assignments

claims.claim: A Power Platform connector is a prebuilt proxy or wrapper around a service API.
claims.quote: Connectors from Microsoft Power Platform act as proxies or "wrappers" around APIs. ... Prebuilt connectors, which are built-in connections to popular services

claims.claim: Power Apps can read and write service data through connectors.
claims.quote: Power Apps retrieves table data into your app and updates data in your data source automatically.

claims.claim: Power Automate uses connectors to communicate with services and perform operations.
claims.quote: They enable Copilot Studio, Power Automate, Power Apps, and Azure Logic Apps to communicate with other apps and services.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio agents use connector operations to retrieve data and perform tasks.
claims.quote: you can connect to various external services and applications to perform a wide range of tasks or retrieve data.

claims.claim: SharePoint, SQL Server and Salesforce are examples of services with Power Platform connectors.
claims.quote: Power Apps has connectors for many popular services and on-premises data sources, including SharePoint, SQL Server, Office 365, Salesforce, and Twitter.

claims.claim: A connection stores authentication credentials for a connector.
claims.quote: Connections are stored authentication credentials for a connector, such as OAuth credentials for the SharePoint connector.

claims.claim: Connector actions and triggers are used through connections.
claims.quote: Custom connectors are used the same way prebuilt connectors are used. You need to create a connection to your API in order to use that connection to call any operations that you expose in your custom connector.

claims.claim: Connectors can provide tables, actions or both.
claims.quote: Some connectors provide only tables, some provide only actions, and some provide both.

claims.claim: The connector reference identifies Standard and Premium connector tiers.
claims.quote: Tier ... Standard ... Premium ... This is a Premium connector for Power Automate and Power Apps or a Standard connector for Azure Logic Apps.

claims.claim: The connector reference identifies Preview and Production release status.
claims.quote: Release Status ... Preview ... Production

claims.claim: The connector reference marks MCP server connectors.
claims.quote: MCP Server connector ... This is an MCP Server connector.

claims.quote: Standard connectors don't require special licensing.

claims.quote: Power Platform use rights included with Microsoft 365 ... A standalone Power Apps or Power Automate plan license is required to access all Premium, on-premises, and custom connectors.

claims.quote: Custom connectors address this scenario by allowing you to create (and even share) a connector with its own triggers and actions. ... A custom connector is a wrapper around a REST API

claims.where: What it is: Kinds of connector

claims.quote: Connectors you create in Power Automate or Power Apps are available in: ... Power Apps

claims.where: What it is: Kinds of connector
claims.claim: Custom connectors created in Power Apps or Power Automate are available in Power Automate cloud flows.

claims.quote: Connectors you create in Power Automate or Power Apps are available in: ... Copilot Studio agents and workflows

claims.where: What it is: Connections and sign-in
claims.claim: SQL Server connections support Microsoft Entra Integrated, SQL Server Authentication and Windows Authentication.
claims.quote: the SQL Server connector allows you to use Microsoft Entra Integrated, SQL Server Authentication, and Windows Authentication.

claims.where: What it is: Connections and sign-in
claims.claim: A shared connection uses the author's credentials implicitly for end users.
claims.quote: the Power Apps author provides the user name and password ... The connection authentication to the data source is then implicitly shared with end users.

claims.where: What it is: A different use of the word
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors were formerly called Microsoft Graph connectors.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors (formerly Microsoft Graph connectors)

claims.where: What it is: A different use of the word
claims.claim: Synced Copilot connectors crawl and index external content into Microsoft Graph.
claims.quote: Synced connectors crawl and index content from external sources into Microsoft Graph.

claims.where: What it is: A different use of the word
claims.claim: Federated Copilot connectors fetch data in real time without indexing it into Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: Federated connectors use an MCP model to fetch data in real time, without indexing content into Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: Data policies classify connectors into Business, Non-Business and Blocked groups.
claims.quote: The three data groups are the Business data group, the Non-Business data group, and the Blocked data group.

claims.claim: Connectors in different data groups cannot be combined in an app or flow.
claims.quote: makers can't create an app or flow that uses both the SharePoint and Gmail connectors. ... connectors in different groups can't share data.

claims.claim: A Blocked connector cannot be used where the data policy applies.
claims.quote: Blocked connectors can't be used where this policy is applied.

claims.claim: A data policy protects only the environments in its scope.
claims.quote: these test environments are now excluded from the policy scope, and the data policy settings are applied to all the remaining (Available) environments.

claims.claim: Microsoft's example allows any connector combination in environments without an applicable data policy.
claims.quote: Because no data policy is applied to test environments, apps and flows can use any set of connectors together in these environments.

claims.claim: A new data policy initially places every connector in Non-Business.
claims.quote: When you create a new policy, all connectors are placed in the Non-Business group by default.

claims.claim: Connector tiers indicate licensing requirements for use.
claims.quote: Class ... Indicates whether connector usage requires a Premium license or is it included in the Built-in/Standard license for Power Platform.

claims.claim: Under Microsoft 365 Power Apps and Power Automate use rights, on-premises connectors require a standalone plan.
claims.quote: A standalone Power Apps or Power Automate plan license is required to access all Premium, on-premises, and custom connectors.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio premium connectors are available in select Copilot Studio plans.
claims.quote: Premium connectors, which are available in select Copilot Studio plans.

claims.claim: An app using a premium connector, custom connector or on-premises gateway is designated Premium.
claims.quote: Premium ... An app that uses at least one premium connector, a custom connector, or an on-premises gateway.

claims.claim: SQL Server was among connectors reclassified as Premium in 2019.
claims.quote: The SQL, Azure, and Dynamics 365 connectors in the following list are now classified as Premium. ... SQL Server ... apps and flows created prior to October 1, 2019

claims.claim: Azure SQL was among connectors reclassified as Premium in 2019.
claims.quote: The SQL, Azure, and Dynamics 365 connectors in the following list are now classified as Premium. ... Azure SQL ... apps and flows created prior to October 1, 2019

claims.claim: Dynamics 365 was among connectors reclassified as Premium in 2019.
claims.quote: The SQL, Azure, and Dynamics 365 connectors in the following list are now classified as Premium. ... Dynamics 365 ... apps and flows created prior to October 1, 2019

claims.claim: The Power Platform FAQ says extended use rights concluded October 1, 2024.
claims.quote: The period for extended use rights concludes on October 1, 2024

claims.claim: The Power Platform FAQ says in-product licensing enforcement begins April 1, 2025.
claims.quote: In-product licensing enforcement begins April 1, 2025

claims.claim: The Power Apps FAQ refers to licensing enforcement beginning February 2027.
claims.quote: prepare for licensing enforcement beginning February 2027.

claims.claim: Microsoft directs readers to the Power Apps pricing guide.
claims.quote: How can I purchase licenses? ... Take a look at the Power Apps pricing guide for details.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends retaining Non-Business as the default group for new connectors.
claims.quote: keep Non-Business as the default group, and manually add services into the Business or Blocked group after your organization evaluates the impact

claims.claim: New nonblockable connectors enter Non-Business when the policy default group is Blocked.
claims.quote: If Microsoft adds any new connectors that can't be blocked and you set the default group for the data policy as Blocked, these connectors are automatically marked as Non-Business instead of Blocked.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Some connectors cannot be blocked
claims.claim: Classic data policies cannot block core connectors such as Dataverse, Approvals and Notifications.
claims.quote: you can't block connectors that drive core Microsoft Power Platform functionality, such as Dataverse, Approvals, and Notifications.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Some connectors cannot be blocked
claims.claim: SharePoint is nonblockable in classic data policies.
claims.quote: For connectors like SharePoint that aren't blockable, the Block action isn't available and a warning appears.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Some connectors cannot be blocked
claims.claim: Nonblockable connectors can be classified as Business or Non-Business.
claims.quote: You can classify these nonblockable connectors into Business or Non-Business data groups.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Some connectors cannot be blocked
claims.claim: ACP can block classic nonblockable connectors on managed environments.
claims.quote: On managed environments (single or environment group), you can block any connector or any action, including those that are nonblockable in classic data policies.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Some connectors cannot be blocked
claims.claim: Nonblockable connectors remain nonblockable under ACP on non-managed environments.
claims.quote: on non-managed environments, the nonblockable connectors remain nonblockable.

claims.claim: Child flows share an internal dependency with the HTTP connector.
claims.quote: child flows share an internal dependency with the HTTP connector

claims.claim: HTTP connector classification can affect child flow execution in the environment or tenant.
claims.quote: the grouping that admins choose for HTTP connectors in a data policy might affect the ability to run child flows in that environment or tenant.

claims.claim: The wildcard custom connector URL pattern defaults to Ignore in new tenant-level policies.
claims.quote: Admins can tag the * pattern to Blocked, Business, Non-business, or Ignore. By default, the pattern is set as Ignore for new data policies.

claims.claim: Ignore defers custom connector classification to other applicable policies.
claims.quote: Ignore ignores data policy classification for all connectors in this tenant-level policy, and defers evaluation of a pattern to other environments or tenant-level policies

claims.claim: Custom connector data policy evaluation occurs before Set Host URL.
claims.quote: Custom connector evaluation with data policies happens before the use of Set Host URL which can dynamically change the custom connector to point to any other REST API. Be sure that custom connectors are built and used by trusted parties.

claims.claim: Set Host URL can dynamically replace a custom connector's host with another REST API.
claims.quote: the host url defined in the connector will no longer be relevant for the correspinding operations since it will always be replaced by the value evaluated by this template.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/connectors/custom-connectors/policy-templates/dynamichosturl/dynamichosturl to sources for the Set Host URL explanation.

claims.claim: Custom connector data policy enforcement does not apply to apps last published before October 2020.
claims.quote: The use of custom connectors isn't enforced by data policies in apps that were last published before October 2020.

claims.claim: Some Power Apps published before October 1, 2020 need republishing for connector action rules to enforce.
claims.quote: Some Power Apps, published before October 1, 2020, need to be republished for connector action rules to enforce data policies.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Advanced connector policies
claims.claim: ACP blocks connectors not explicitly allowed.
claims.quote: ACP enforces a strict allowlist ... every connector that isn't explicitly allowed is blocked.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Advanced connector policies
claims.claim: ACP takes effect on saving a single-environment policy or publishing environment group rules.
claims.quote: ACP enforces a strict allowlist as soon as you save it (single environment) or publish it (environment group)

claims.claim: ACP currently supports certified connectors only.
claims.quote: Advanced connector policies currently apply to certified connectors only.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Advanced connector policies
claims.claim: ACP does not currently support custom connectors.
claims.quote: Custom connectors ... Not yet supported ... Use classic data policies for custom connector governance.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Advanced connector policies
claims.claim: ACP does not currently support HTTP connectors.
claims.quote: HTTP connectors ... Not yet supported ... Use classic data policies and connector endpoint filtering for HTTP governance.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Advanced connector policies
claims.claim: ACP design-time enforcement is rolling out across maker portals.
claims.quote: Design-time enforcement is rolling out across maker portals in the following order

claims.where: Risks and limits: Advanced connector policies
claims.claim: ACP enforcement is runtime-only for workloads whose maker portal lacks design-time support.
claims.quote: Until design-time support is available in a given maker portal, ACP operates as a runtime-only enforcement for that workload.

claims.claim: Newly created shared connections are secured after January 2024.
claims.quote: after January 2024, all newly created shared connections are secured.

claims.claim: Earlier apps using shared connections need republishing to secure them.
claims.quote: To secure existing apps, republish them. ... If you have an app using the connections published before January 2024, republish your application

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends at most 10 connectors per canvas app.
claims.quote: Keep the number of connectors in a canvas app to a maximum of 10

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends no more than 20 connection references per canvas app.
claims.quote: connection references to no more than 20.

claims.claim: Exceeding the connector and connection reference recommendations can increase loading times and cause saving problems.
claims.quote: Going beyond these limits can lead to longer loading times for users when launching the app and can cause problems when saving the app.

claims.claim: Environment-level policies in environments with a Dataverse database require System Administrator instead of Environment Admin.
claims.quote: For environments with a Dataverse database, you need to be assigned the System Administrator role instead.

claims.claim: Environment admins cannot edit tenant-created data policies.
claims.quote: Environment admins can't edit policies created by the tenant admin.

claims.claim: Environment admins cannot delete tenant-created data policies.
claims.quote: Environment admins can't delete policies created by the tenant admin.

claims.claim: Environment-level data policies cannot override tenant-wide data policies.
claims.quote: Environment-level data policies can't override tenant-wide data policies.

claims.claim: ACP starts in mixed mode alongside classic data policies.
claims.quote: Mixed mode is the default state when you first enable ACP: classic data policies continue to be evaluated alongside your new advanced connector policy

claims.claim: Mixed mode enforces the most restrictive settings from ACP and classic data policies.
claims.quote: a combined policy that merges the most restrictive settings from both classic data policies and ACP to provide full enforcement.

claims.claim: ACP-only mode ignores classic data policies for its scope.
claims.quote: All classic data policies are ignored for those environments, even if they're still configured.

claims.claim: ACP-only mode does not delete classic data policies.
claims.quote: Data policy configurations aren't deleted. They remain in place but aren't enforced while ACP-only mode is active.

claims.claim: Classic data policies provide connector action control.
claims.quote: Select an existing policy ... Edit policy ... In the Prebuilt connectors section, select a Blockable connector ... Use the side panel to allow or deny specific actions.

claims.claim: Endpoint filtering remains a classic data policy feature.
claims.quote: Endpoints that a connector can reach ... Classic data policies with connector endpoint filtering ... Not available in ACP.

claims.claim: Get-AdminPowerAppConnection returns connections across environments where the caller is an environment admin.
claims.quote: Get-AdminPowerAppConnection ... Returns all connections from all environments where the calling user is an environment admin. For global admins, this searches across all environments in the tenant.

claims.claim: Get-AdminPowerAppConnector lists custom connector details in the tenant.
claims.quote: Get-AdminPowerAppConnector ... Returns a list of all custom connector details in the tenant.

claims.claim: Get-AdminPowerAppConnector does not list custom connectors in solutions.
claims.quote: Get-AdminPowerAppConnector doesn't list custom connectors that are in a solution. This is a known limitation.

claims.claim: Enforcing data policies on connections disables existing violating connections.
claims.quote: Enforcing disables existing connections that violate data policies and enables any previously disabled connections that no longer violate data policies.

claims.where: Open questions: custom and HTTP connectors
claims.claim: Microsoft plans future ACP support for custom and HTTP connectors without specifying a release date.
claims.quote: Custom connector and HTTP connector support are planned for a future date as a separate rule type.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans future admin center support for individual triggers in classic connector action control.
claims.quote: Support is planned for the Power Platform admin center in the future.

claims.claim: ACP general availability is tied to each workload's maker portal design-time enforcement release.
claims.quote: Each maker portal's release of design-time enforcement for ACP marks the general availability of ACP for that workload.
